title: 07. Advanced & Agentic RAG: Connecting MCP to Google ADK

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: **In the last lesson** we used LangGraph. **Today** we connect our MCP server to **Google ADK** — Google's own agent framework.

sections.title: ① Real-World Analogy — The Universal Power Adapter
sections.body:
When you travel to a different country, your device's plug might not fit the wall socket. A **universal adapter** lets your device work anywhere.

Google ADK has its own way of defining tools. Your MCP server has its own format. `MCPToolset` is the universal adapter — it converts your MCP tools into Google ADK tools automatically.

sections.title: ② Plain English Explanation
sections.body:
**Google ADK** (Agent Development Kit) is Google's framework for building AI agents. It is designed to work with Google's Gemini models. Like LangChain, it has its own tool format — but it supports MCP natively through a class called `MCPToolset`.

`MCPToolset` connects to your MCP server, discovers its tools automatically, and makes them available to any Google ADK agent. The agent can then use your MCP tools exactly like native Google ADK tools.

sections.title: ③ Installation
sections.body:
```bash
# Install Google ADK
pip install google-adk

# You also need a Google API key for Gemini
# Set it in your environment:
# export GOOGLE_API_KEY="your-google-api-key-here"
```

sections.title: ④ Complete Code Example
sections.body:
```python
# google_adk_mcp.py
# Connect Google ADK to your FastMCP calculator server
# Install: pip install google-adk
# Requires: GOOGLE_API_KEY environment variable

import asyncio
import os
from google.adk.agents import LlmAgent              # Google ADK's LLM agent
from google.adk.tools.mcp_tool.mcp_toolset import MCPToolset  # The MCP bridge
from google.adk.runners import Runner               # Executes the agent
from google.adk.sessions import InMemorySessionService  # Manages session state

# ─── STEP 1: Set up configuration ────────────────────────────────────

APP_NAME = "calculator_app"    # Name for our application
USER_ID = "veera"             # Simulated user ID
SESSION_ID = "session_001"    # Simulated session ID

# ─── STEP 2: Main async function ─────────────────────────────────────

async def run_google_adk_agent():
    """
    Create a Google ADK agent connected to our MCP server
    and have it answer math questions.
    """
    print("🚀 Setting up Google ADK agent with MCP tools...")
    
    # MCPToolset connects to our MCP server and loads its tools
    # It uses StdioServerParameters under the hood (same as our client in Lesson 9)
    mcp_toolset = MCPToolset(
        connection_params={
            "command": "python",                    # How to start the server
            "args": ["fastmcp_full_server.py"],     # Which server script
        }
    )
    
    # ── STEP 3: Create the ADK Agent ──────────────────────────────────
    
    # LlmAgent is Google ADK's main agent type
    agent = LlmAgent(
        name="MathAssistant",
        model="gemini-2.0-flash",       # Gemini model to use
        description="A math assistant that can perform calculations",
        instruction="""
        You are a helpful math assistant.
        When the user asks a math question, use the available calculator tools.
        Always show your work — explain which tool you used and what it returned.
        Be friendly and encouraging.
        """,
        tools=[mcp_toolset],            # Provide the MCP toolset to the agent
    )
    
    # ── STEP 4: Set up the runner ──────────────────────────────────────
    
    # InMemorySessionService manages conversation state
    session_service = InMemorySessionService()
    
    # Create a session for our user
    await session_service.create_session(
        app_name=APP_NAME,
        user_id=USER_ID,
        session_id=SESSION_ID
    )
    
    # Runner connects the agent, session service, and handles execution
    runner = Runner(
        agent=agent,
        app_name=APP_NAME,
        session_service=session_service
    )
    
    # ── STEP 5: Ask questions ──────────────────────────────────────────
    
    from google.adk.types import Content, Part   # Message types for Google ADK
    
    questions = [
        "What is 567 times 89?",
        "If I have 1000 and spend 375, how much is left?",
        "What is 2 to the power of 10? (use multiply repeatedly if needed)"
    ]
    
    for question in questions:
        print(f"\n{'='*55}")
        print(f"Q: {question}")
        print(f"{'='*55}")
        
        # Create a user message in ADK format
        user_message = Content(
            role="user",
            parts=[Part(text=question)]
        )
        
        # Run the agent and collect the response
        final_response = None
        
        async for event in runner.run_async(
            user_id=USER_ID,
            session_id=SESSION_ID,
            new_message=user_message
        ):
            # Events come in as the agent thinks and acts
            # We want the final text response
            if event.is_final_response():
                if event.content and event.content.parts:
                    final_response = event.content.parts[0].text
        
        if final_response:
            print(f"A: {final_response}")
        else:
            print("A: (no response received)")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Check for API key
    if not os.getenv("GOOGLE_API_KEY"):
        print("❌ Please set GOOGLE_API_KEY environment variable")
        print("   export GOOGLE_API_KEY='your-api-key'")
        exit(1)
    
    asyncio.run(run_google_adk_agent())
```

sections.title: ⑥ Quick Recap — What Did We Just Learn?
sections.body:
- ✅ Google ADK uses `MCPToolset` to connect to MCP servers natively
- ✅ `LlmAgent` with `tools=[mcp_toolset]` creates a Gemini-powered MCP agent
- ✅ `Runner` executes the agent and manages the request/response lifecycle
- ✅ Tool discovery is automatic — no need to list tools manually
- ✅ The same MCP server works with LangChain, LangGraph, AND Google ADK

🎉 **Three frameworks down! One more to go — OpenAI Agents SDK!**
